claim: The combination of knowledgeable grounding, collective deliberation, and multi-criteria decision-making is sufficient to produce a systematic and robust assessment of a research idea.
source_excerpt: A systematic and robust assessment of a research idea is achieved through a process that combines knowledgeable grounding against existing work, collective deliberation from diverse perspectives, and multi-criteria decision-making.

claim: The final decisions from a peer-review process (e.g., Reject, Poster, Spotlight, Oral) constitute a valid, "inherent ground-truth ranking" of the quality of the underlying research ideas.
source_excerpt: This process will yield groups of ideas with an inherent ground-truth ranking, from which we can also derive pair-wise comparison tasks.

claim: An automated extraction agent is capable of converting full research papers into a structured format that accurately represents the core research idea for evaluation.
source_excerpt: We will use an extraction agent to convert these papers into a structured idea format, followed by manual verification.

claim: The performance of an idea evaluation system can be meaningfully measured by framing it as a classification task and using standard metrics like Accuracy and macro F1 score.
source_excerpt: We will frame this as a classification problem (binary: Accept/Reject; ternary: Reject/Poster/Highlight) and measure performance using Accuracy and macro F1 score.

claim: The "innovation review board" (a simulated panel of diverse personas) is a necessary component that provides a significant benefit over using a single LLM-as-a-Judge.
source_excerpt: To confirm the contribution of each component, we will conduct several ablation studies, including ... replacing the innovation review board with a single LLM-as-a-Judge...
